newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * The leaders of the Democratic Convention and Social Dmocratic Union signed a cooperation protocol to back Emil Constantinescu in the run-off against Preisdent Ion Iliescu on November 17.
The CDR will designate the chairman of the lower Chamber of Deputies and USD the chairman of the upper house, the Senate.
The CDR will take the Prime Minister portfolio and USD the deputy prime minister. The USD also receives at least one ministry in each of the economic, social-cultural and public order sectors.

* The leaders of two liberal parties, members of the opposition Democratic Convention (CDR), signed a joint document appealing to all liberal parties to unite in a strong Liberal party inside the CDR.

* Miron Mitrea, general secretary of the ruling Party of Social Democracy, said a CDR government would make a serious error by giving the Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR) deputy minister the education and culture ministries and the local prefect posts in the counties of Covasna, Harghita and Mures.
Mitrea said that "handing power means to UDMR is extremely serious and affects the national security".
* The Central Electoral Bureau (BEC) released final results in November 3 parliament and presidential elections.
Results put President Ion Iliescu ahead with 32.25 percent, followed by Emil Constantinescu with 28.21 percent, Petre Roman with 20.54 percent and Gyorgy Frunda with 6.02 percent.

The opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) bloc leads in both houses of parliament with 30.70 percent in the Senate and 30.17 percent in the lower Chamber of Deputies. The Party of Social Democracy is second with 23.08 percent and 21.52 percent.
The third political group in parliament is the Social Democratic Union (USD) which got 13.16 percent of votes in the Senate and 12.93 percent in the lower house.
*The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development granted Romania a new tranche of a loan to modernise the Bucharest-Pitesti highway. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
